gate_reasoning: Stage 3 scores 71.4% of claims as Low confidence (50 of 70 scored claims), with only 11 High-confidence claims (15.7%) — all of which are concentrated in regulatory filings (Samsara 10-K, Karooooo 20-F), government statistics (FMCSA), and two industry association reports (BSI/TT Club, ReCAAP ISC). The stage fails on three structural deficiencies that cannot be remediated by minor additions: first, the most load-bearing quantified claim in Pain Point 3.1 — the 30–40% industry average visibility compliance rate — is sourced exclusively from a competing vendor's marketing site with zero independent corroboration, which means the entire $800M–$1.6B broker-revenue-at-risk calculation rests on uncorroborated vendor data; second, the 15–25% insurance premium penalty claim in Pain Point 3.2 is sourced from an IoT vendor's marketing blog with no actuarial or underwriting primary source; third, the $35B pharma cold-chain loss figure is factually misattributed to IATA when the actual source is IQVIA (2019), requiring a correction before the figure can be cited at any confidence level. Additionally, the draft incorrectly rates the Berg Insight SEA fleet data (VC-8) as High confidence when the correct score under the rubric is Low — Berg Insight is a niche paid research firm distributed via press releases, not a top-tier consultancy authored report. Deep research should target five specific gaps: (1) neutral third-party benchmark for RTTVP visibility compliance rates; (2) IUMI or Lloyd's actuarial data for cold-chain premium differentials; (3) direct IQVIA and IATA source citation correction for the $35B figure; (4) government statistics cross-validation of the 17.5% SEA telematics penetration rate; (5) ASEAN multilateral or ADB source for the $119.4B road freight market size.
